source_note: Two cross-subtopic authored assessments; scores are unreviewed author proposals; original exam custody not asserted.

tasks.title: Reaction ledger under incomplete observation
tasks.prompt: A 2.4 g magnesium ribbon is heated in a partly open crucible. The final residue reads 3.5 g. A pale smoke escaped and oxygen was supplied from surrounding air. A second student writes 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO and concludes the result disproves conservation because the residue gain is less than the 1.6 g expected for complete 2.4 g Mg oxidation. Explain what material boundaries are missing, which mass quantities can actually be inferred, and design two measurements that discriminate incomplete reaction from escaping product.
tasks.post_commit_worked_answer: The 2.4 g Mg sample can incorporate oxygen from outside the measured crucible. Under complete conversion to MgO the added oxygen would be 1.6 g and 4.0 g product would be retained if no material escaped. The measured 3.5 g residue is 0.5 g below that prediction. But the record gives neither retained unreacted Mg nor mass of escaping MgO smoke, so it does not determine whether the conversion was complete. A covered/filtered collection system to capture aerosol and an independent chemical analysis of residue (Mg versus MgO) distinguish the hypotheses. Mass conservation applies to Mg plus oxygen plus all products; the open residue reading is not the closed-system total.
tasks.protected_work: Choose the scientific model and independently reconcile at least two representations or observations, including a credible alternative or boundary.

factor_evidence.concept_model_selection: Choose between complete conversion, escape and incomplete conversion models.
factor_evidence.representation_translation: Translate measured crucible mass to a closed Mg–O–smoke ledger.
factor_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Link initial mass, stoichiometric oxygen uptake, and missing product.
factor_evidence.trap_exception_sensitivity: A mass deficit can coexist with oxygen uptake, challenging a naive conservation claim.

self_score_proposal.qualification_note: Not independently QRT-adjudicated. Difficulty may be downgraded if task is not intrinsically high demand or if scaffolding reveals the decisive work.

tasks.title: A white precipitate—two conflicting investigations
tasks.prompt: Lab A mixes BaCl₂(aq) and Na₂SO₄(aq) and reports a white solid. Lab B mixes an unknown colourless salt solution with the same sulfate reagent, also reports a white solid, but after filtration a fresh barium-ion test on the filtrate is positive. A student concludes that both white solids are pure BaSO₄ and that the positive barium test proves excess BaSO₄ had dissolved. Build two competing species ledgers consistent with the observations, identify which part of the conclusion is unsupported, and propose an experiment that can separate residual dissolved Ba²⁺ from a second unidentified precipitate. Do not assume the unknown solution is pure.
tasks.post_commit_worked_answer: For A the plausible net precipitation Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → BaSO₄(s) conserves charge and species; Na⁺/Cl⁻ are spectators. For B the solid may include BaSO₄ if Ba²⁺ was initially present, but the unknown could contain another cation forming an insoluble sulfate or a contaminant. A positive dissolved barium test after filtration does not establish dissolution of the precipitate; it may instead reflect unreacted Ba²⁺ because sulfate was limiting, or imperfect separation/other interference. Compare measured starting Ba²⁺ and sulfate amounts, test filtered solids using suitable independently reviewed chemical methods, and perform stoichiometric/blank controls. Under no condition does a common colour alone establish a unique species. It is ungrounded to declare 'excess BaSO₄ dissolved' from a positive Ba²⁺ filtrate result.
tasks.protected_work: Choose the scientific model and independently reconcile at least two representations or observations, including a credible alternative or boundary.

factor_evidence.concept_model_selection: Multiple competing precipitation/solubility and limitation models.
factor_evidence.representation_translation: Translate observed white solid and filtrate test to two ionic-phase ledgers.
factor_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Constrain species before and after filtration, then test the original inference.
factor_evidence.algebra_computational_load: No advanced algebra; the difficulty is conceptual evidence reconciliation.
factor_evidence.trap_exception_sensitivity: A barium signal after filtration reverses the familiar 'all barium went to precipitate' inference.
